Foil Postcards for Promos & Announcements That Shimmer & Shine


Use foil postcards to delight and dazzle your customers. Foil printing adds reflective, shiny highlights to your postcards, making the extra glamorous message or image impossible to ignore. If you’re planning to launch a direct mail campaign, adding shimmering foil elements to your postcards will help increase response rates and cultivate a positive impression of your brand.

Metallic Shine for Maximum Impact

Vibrant Foil Colors
Premium Cardstock Options
Postcard Sizes for Any Campaign
Choose from gold, silver, copper, black, blue, or red foil Printed on 14 pt. uncoated, 16 pt. gloss, or silk laminated cardstock  Available in 4" x 6", 5" x 7", and other standard postcard sizes
Highlight key text, logos, or calls-to-action Silk lamination adds softness and water resistance Rounded corners optional for a modern look
Adds shine and sophistication to any design Spot UV available for added contrast Suitable for mailing, handouts, or packaging inserts

Create a Postcard That Reflects Premium Branding





Choose From Six Foil Colors

Gold, silver, copper, red, blue, and black foil options available for custom accents.

Select Your Finish

Go with silk lamination for a luxe feel, gloss for shine, or uncoated for a writable surface.

Add Spot UV for Contrast

Combine foil with high-gloss spot UV to highlight other design elements.

Rounded Corners Optional

Choose rounded edges for a smooth, modern finish.

Multiple Sizes Available

Choose from popular formats like 4" x 6" and 5" x 7" for direct mail or in-store displays.



Foil Postcards FAQs

Q: Should I print on 14 pt. or 16 pt. cardstock?

Your choice will depend on the thickness and appearance you’re aiming for in the design. The 14 pt. cardstock is the standard choice seen in most business cards. This is recommended for anyone on a budget but who wants to exude reliability in their message.

The 16 pt. cardstock is slightly thicker and prone to less rigidity. It also comes with a silk lamination that increases its overall thickness. Recommended for those with a higher budget and who need to invest in a luxury design.

 

Q: How do I prepare a file for spot UV printing?

The spot UV area should be in a separate vector layer on your file. If you can’t separate it in a vector layer, contact customer service and let them know you’re sending a second file that shows the spot UV area in a different color.

Q: Do I save more with bulk printing?

Yes, the larger your order quantity, the less you spend on each postcard. The online calculator will show the total and unit price based on your specifications.
